# Groz.Nail

> Russian manicure studio based in Round Rock, Texas. Julia Grozova's private nail studio on Gattis School Rd in Round Rock. Meticulous e-file cuticle work, gel that lasts, and art that runs from milky pearl to teal chrome stilettos. By appointment only.

## Services
- Russian manicure: Precise e-file prep and meticulous cuticle work, then shaping and a smooth gel finish that sits close to the cuticle and grows out clean. New to it? Start with the new-client visit and a consultation.
- Russian dry pedicure: A dry pedicure with no soaking: thorough cuticle care, clean shaping and callus treatment with a Smart Disc, finished in gel if you like. Pedicure fixes welcome.
- Extensions & nail art: Sculpted extensions in the shape you want, plus chrome and cat eye, French, ombre and stamping as add-ons to any manicure.

## About
Groz.Nail is Julia Grozova's private studio in Suite 410 on Gattis School Rd in Round Rock: one chair, one client at a time, by appointment only. Julia started doing nails about five years ago at the windowsill of her apartment in Yekaterinburg, Russia. She trained, took models at home and built a client list, and now runs her own cozy studio here in Texas. The work is built on the Russian manicure: careful e-file prep, cuticle work that leaves nothing to pick at, and gel that sits close and grows out neatly. First-timers who were nervous about the e-file keep saying the same thing: she is delicate and careful. Every client gets fresh single-use files and buffers, and metal tools go through medical-grade sterilization. Quality over quantity, healthy nails first.

## Frequently asked questions
- Q: What is a Russian manicure?
  A: A detailed manicure where the cuticle area is cleaned with an electric file instead of only pushing and clipping. Done carefully, it lets the gel sit very close to the cuticle, so the manicure looks clean and grows out neatly.
- Q: How much does it cost?
  A: A Signature Russian Manicure is $70 without gel and $120 with gel on short to medium nails ($145 for long nails). First visit? The New Client Russian Manicure is $90 and starts with a consultation. The full menu is on the Services page.
- Q: Does the e-file hurt?
  A: It should not. Several clients mention they were nervous about the e-file and found Julia extremely delicate and careful. Speak up right away if anything feels uncomfortable and she will adjust.
- Q: What is a dry pedicure?
  A: The Signature Russian Pedicure is done without soaking in water: thorough cuticle care, shaping and callus treatment with a Smart Disc, with or without gel.
- Q: Can you fix a bad manicure or pedicure?
  A: Yes. Clients have come in with an at-home gel nightmare or a pedicure that went wrong elsewhere and left with a clean, corrected set. Removal of gel ($15) or acrylic and dip ($25) from another salon is booked as a separate add-on.
- Q: Are there any offers?
  A: Yes: 10% off your first visit, $15 off during your birthday month, and $20 off every Wednesday (limited availability).
- Q: How often should I come back?
  A: Julia recommends refreshing gel about every 4 weeks. In between, use cuticle oil and avoid picking or peeling the gel.
- Q: How do I book?
  A: Groz.Nail is by appointment only. Book online to see every open time; designs are add-ons, so pick them when you book so extra time is set aside.
